subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup move from pairing by default to token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom while preserving explicit pairing-mode configs?
rationale: This is a bounded implementation shape, but it changes Telegram first-run trust, owner identity capture, and the default authorization boundary for a discoverable bot.

options.title: Adopt verified owner capture
options.body: Generate a short setup token, accept only the matching Telegram message as owner proof, write allowlist config for fresh or implicit setups, and preserve explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Defer to cross-channel defaults
options.body: Keep this issue open but settle the broader post-bootstrap channel policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81876 before changing Telegram setup.

options.title: Keep pairing default
options.body: Document pairing as the intentional first-run default and leave owner-only Telegram access as explicit manual allowlist setup.

recommendation.title: Adopt verified owner capture
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, accept only the matching Telegram message as owner proof, write allowlist config for fresh or implicit setups, and preserve explicit pairing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from prior product/security review context and Telegram runtime/docs/setup history.
